clue.text: In Lourdes, become member of a Catholic society

parts.note: in Lourdes, a French town, the word for I is je
to become someone is to suit them, as a hat suits you

explanation.surface: Someone visiting the French pilgrimage town decides to join a religious order.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR dropped the 'I' that the wordplay needs: French JE for 'I', then SUIT in the sense 'look good on'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Society of Jesus is a Catholic order whose members are called by this name.

clue.text: Fish from can, baked with tiny bit of oil added

parts.note: can and john are both slang for a toilet

indicators.note: added says the small piece is put into the other word

parts.note: baked means dried out

indicators.note: a tiny bit of oil is just its first letter

explanation.surface: A tinned fish cooked in the oven with a drop of oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like a tin, but it is US slang for a lavatory, JOHN. 'added' puts O (the first letter of 'oil', from 'tiny bit of') into DRY.
explanation.definitionFit: This flat sea fish with a dark spot on each side is prized for eating.

clue.text: Pages and pages of numbers?

parts.note: numbers here are songs or musical items, not figures, so the pages are a collection of tunes

explanation.definitionFit: A book of songs runs to many pages of musical items, each called a number.

clue.text: Leaders of Islam meeting at mosques sometimes

definitions.text: Leaders of Islam meeting at mosques sometimes

indicators.note: leaders of means the first letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Islamic prayer leaders sometimes gather at mosques.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening letters of 'Islam meeting at mosques sometimes' spell the answer, and the whole clue also describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: These Muslim clerics lead prayers in mosques and so are leaders of the faith.

clue.text: Sparkling, say, then largely composed for examination

indicators.note: say tells us a word spoken aloud gives letters spelt another way

parts.note: sparkling drinks are fizzy

indicators.note: largely means most of the word but not all, losing its final letter

parts.note: composed means calm

explanation.surface: A bubbly drink, then a mostly calm mood, before a doctor's check-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sparkling' is FIZZY, which said aloud gives PHYSI; 'largely' cuts the last letter from CALM to leave CAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical check-up of the body is called a physical, a noun sense of the word.

clue.text: Very quickly surrender fighter planes at end of conflict

parts.note: to surrender something is to hand it over
the Mirage F1 is a fighter plane, so several are F1s, with the 1 read as I

indicators.note: at end of means the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Air forces hand over their jets as the war ends.
explanation.walkthrough: Mirage F1s give FIS, with the digit 1 read as letter I; 'at end of' takes T from 'conflict'.
explanation.definitionFit: Making money hand over fist means earning it fast and in large amounts.

clue.text: This is manufactured with local fabric

indicators.note: is manufactured means made or put together, so the letters are assembled anew

explanation.surface: A cloth produced from local material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is manufactured' rearranges THIS plus LOCAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Canvas made for ships' sails is a strong cloth.

clue.text: In island socialist reveals beliefs

indicators.note: in says the socialist is placed inside the island's name

parts.note: Cos is a Greek island
a red is a socialist or communist

explanation.surface: On a Greek isle a left-winger lays out what they believe.
explanation.walkthrough: COS, also spelt Kos, is a Greek island in the Dodecanese.
explanation.definitionFit: Credos are statements of faith or principles.

clue.text: Musician included in catalogue of names is unknown, right?

indicators.note: included in says these letters go inside the catalogue

parts.note: a catalogue of names is a list
Y is a mathematical unknown, like x

explanation.surface: A performer asks whether it's correct that they're anonymous in the roll.
explanation.walkthrough: Y, an algebraic unknown, and R, right, go inside LIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A lyrist plays the lyre, or writes lyrics.

clue.text: Ailing nag housed in mostly cold, large building

indicators.note: housed in says the nag's letters are lodged inside another word
mostly means one letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a haar is a cold sea fog on the east coast of Britain

indicators.note: ailing means sick, so the letters of nag are in poor shape and rearranged

explanation.surface: A sick old horse is kept in a chilly barn.
explanation.walkthrough: A haar is a cold sea mist in Scotland and north-east England. 'mostly' drops one of its two As, and 'housed in' takes the anagram (signalled by 'Ailing') of the old horse inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Aircraft are kept in this kind of big shed at an airfield.

clue.text: Cricketer's manoeuvre

explanation.surface: A player's tactical move on the cricket field.
explanation.walkthrough: Farokh Engineer was a famous Indian wicketkeeper-batsman of the 1960s and 70s; the 's stands for 'is', linking the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Farokh Engineer kept wicket for India; to manoeuvre something is to contrive or arrange it cleverly.

clue.text: Drunk at end of session refusing to move

indicators.note: at end of means the drunk word follows the session word

parts.note: a session of a court or parliament is a sitting
drunk means tight

explanation.surface: Someone tipsy when the meeting finishes won't budge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' looks like the start of the definition, but it is wordplay; 'at end of' puts it after the session word.
explanation.definitionFit: Staying put and not reacting, holding one's position, is the idiom here.

clue.text: Newspaper employee briefly turns to alight

indicators.note: turns says the short title for the newspaper worker is read from its end back

parts.note: a sub-editor at a newspaper is called a sub-ed for short

explanation.surface: A journalist on a short shift switches to getting off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' reads SUBED backwards; 'briefly' tells you the employee is the short form sub-ed, not sub-editor.
explanation.definitionFit: To get off a coach or bus is to debus, as soldiers or passengers dismount.

clue.text: Retired soldiers and I scorn ridiculously small medal

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn or drawn back, so the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

indicators.note: ridiculously says the letters of scorn are put into a silly new order

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Old soldiers and I sneer at a tiny decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' reads the other-ranks abbreviation backwards, and 'ridiculously' rearranges 'scorn'. The I comes first in the answer even though 'and I' follows the soldiers in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: This German military decoration for bravery was awarded in both world wars.

clue.text: Bounder abridged gospel writer's finest book

parts.note: a bounder here is something that bounds: a kangaroo, roo for short

indicators.note: abridged means shortened, so the evangelist's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Matthew wrote the first gospel
the finest is the top

explanation.surface: A cad's shortened version of a gospel is the best volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bounder' looks like a cad but is a jumping kangaroo, ROO. It is John Braine's 1957 novel.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1957 novel by John Braine follows the social climber Joe Lampton.

clue.text: Adults about to take leave in eastern part of

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Adults about to take leave in eastern part of (9)' is cut short: the definition needs a country after 'part of' (France); AA around QUIT + IN + E gives the letters, but no scan or search gives the missing word.
annotationWithheld.clue: Adults about to take leave in eastern part of

clue.text: Occasion for celebrating: European politician's introduced new strategy

indicators.note: introduced means brought in, so the politician enters the celebration

parts.note: a gala is a festive occasion
an MEP is a Member of the European Parliament

explanation.surface: At a celebration a Euro MP unveils a fresh strategy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introduced' puts the Euro MP inside the festive occasion, and the abbreviation for new follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A game plan is a planned course of action.

clue.text: Italian poetry: one's into that

indicators.note: into means the word one goes inside the poetry word

parts.note: poetry is verse
one's is read as one is, giving just the word one

explanation.surface: Italian poetry: someone keen on that.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'one's into that' as 'one is into that': 'into' places the word inside the poetry. Paolo Veronese was a Venetian Renaissance painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Veronese means from Verona, and is also the name of the Renaissance painter Paolo Veronese.

clue.text: Sherpa's peculiar expression?

parts.note: the word Sherpa is what you get when the letters of phrase are turned about and rearranged

explanation.surface: A Himalayan guide has an odd way of saying things.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as wordplay: a turn (rearrangement) of PHRASE makes SHERPA, which is what the clue shows.
explanation.definitionFit: A turn of phrase is a particular way of expressing something in words.

clue.text: Man: a British island

parts.note: to man a ship or desk is to staff it

explanation.surface: The Isle of Man is a British island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like the Isle of Man, but it is a verb, to staff. Staffa is a small Hebridean island with Fingal's Cave.
explanation.definitionFit: Staffa is a small island in the Inner Hebrides of Scotland.

clue.text: Territory seen going through Canada, venturing northwards

indicators.note: northwards says the hidden letters are read backwards
seen going through says the letters are found passing through the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A region seen while travelling through Canada and heading north.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'seen going through' in the definition, but it signals the hidden letters; in a down clue 'northwards' reads them upward. Nevada was a US territory before statehood.
explanation.definitionFit: Nevada Territory was a US territory from 1861 before becoming a state.

clue.text: Time delays, as one leaves America

indicators.note: leaves means goes away from, so a letter departs from the word

parts.note: to delay is to hesitate
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Time drags as someone departs for the USA.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' removes I (one) from HESITATES to leave HESTATES.
explanation.definitionFit: The United States is often called by this short informal name.

clue.text: Spanish fellow that is bitten by wild dog

indicators.note: bitten by says one piece is held between the jaws of another
wild says the letters of dog run riot into a new order

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A Spaniard gets nipped by a feral hound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' scrambles the hound's three letters, and 'bitten by' holds the Latin abbreviation for 'that is' in their jaws.
explanation.definitionFit: Diego is a common Spanish man's name, as in Diego Velazquez.

clue.text: Furrow initially dug close to running water

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the word dug

parts.note: a rill is a small stream

explanation.surface: A trench first dug beside a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: D, the first letter of 'dug', goes next to RILL.
explanation.definitionFit: A drill is a small furrow made for sowing seeds.

clue.text: Burning with love for a bird

parts.note: burning means flaming
love is zero in tennis, looking like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone ablaze with passion for a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bird' suggests a girlfriend in British slang, but it is the pink wading bird.
explanation.definitionFit: This pink long-legged wading bird is named for its flame colour.

clue.text: Young female doctor turning back on romance

indicators.note: turning back tells us to read the word from its end to its start

parts.note: to doctor results is to rig them
to romance is to exaggerate or lie

explanation.surface: A woman doctor returns to a love affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' is the verb, RIG, which 'turning back' makes GIR; 'romance' is also a verb, to tell tall tales, LIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Girlie is an informal word for a young woman or girl.

clue.text: An assortment of tales — about a hundred -in literary collections

indicators.note: in says the abbreviation sits inside the rearranged letters
an assortment is a mixed set, so the letters of tales are mixed

parts.note: C stands for circa, about, and is also the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A mixed bag of around a hundred stories in a literary anthology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assortment of' rearranges 'tales', and 'in' puts the single letter for 'about a hundred' within it, after the opening 'An'.
explanation.definitionFit: Analects are selected extracts, most famously the sayings of Confucius gathered by his followers.

clue.text: Look here, A level exam covers most of the country

indicators.note: covers means wraps around, so the exam's letters go round the other piece

parts.note: A level was taken for the GCE, the General Certificate of Education

indicators.note: most of means all but the final letter

parts.note: the country is the land

explanation.surface: An exam paper surveying most of the nation, offered with a 'look here'.
explanation.walkthrough: A levels are English school-leaving exams, part of the GCE. 'most of' trims LAND to LAN, which GCE covers.
explanation.definitionFit: A glance is a quick look.
